headline: Claude's 8 Secret Prompt Codes Revealed
summary: Discover the hidden prompt patterns that unlock Claude's full potential. 90% of users miss these architectural techniques for controlling model behavior, reasoning depth, and output structure.

slides.title: Why Your Claude Outputs Feel Inconsistent
slides.subtitle: 90% of developers treat prompting as trial-and-error, not engineering.
slides.body: Most teams waste hours tweaking prompts blindly. The real problem? Missing the control codes that steer model behavior predictably.
slides.deep_dive: Large language models appear stochastic, but they follow deterministic patterns when given structural signals. These signals — system prompts, formatting constraints, reasoning scaffolds — act as architectural guardrails. Without them, you're debugging chaos. With them, you're designing reliable AI systems.
slides.key_fact: 90% of Claude users don't know these 8 control patterns exist.
slides.why_it_matters: Transforms prompting from art into repeatable engineering discipline.

slides.title: Prompt Patterns Are Compiler Flags for LLMs
slides.subtitle: Each code flips a behavioral switch inside the model.
slides.body: Think of patterns as compiler flags: --reason-deep, --format-json, --role-expert. They don't change the model — they change how it executes your request.
slides.deep_dive: The model weights are fixed. What changes is the activation path triggered by your prompt structure. A 'think step by step' pattern activates sequential reasoning circuits. A 'respond in XML' pattern constrains the output distribution. You're not asking differently — you're routing computation differently.
slides.key_fact: Patterns route model computation; they don't add knowledge.
slides.why_it_matters: Enables predictable, testable AI behavior in production systems.

slides.title: From Raw Prompt to Engineered Control
slides.subtitle: Input structure determines which model capabilities activate.
slides.body: Same question, different structural wrapper, radically different output quality and reliability.
slides.deep_dive: A bare prompt like 'Analyze this code' triggers default chat behavior — conversational, variable depth. Wrap it with 'You are a senior engineer. Think step by step. Output JSON with severity, line, fix' and you activate: role conditioning, chain-of-thought reasoning, and structured output constraints simultaneously. Three control codes, one predictable result.
slides.key_fact: Structure routes computation; content provides context.
slides.why_it_matters: Eliminates output variance without changing model or temperature.
slides.processing: Applies 3 control codes: role + reasoning + format

slides.title: Every Control Code Has a Cost
slides.subtitle: Latency, context, and flexibility compete for your token budget.
slides.body: Deeper reasoning costs tokens. Strict formats reduce creativity. Role prompts consume context window.
slides.deep_dive: Chain-of-thought adds 3-5x token overhead for complex tasks. XML formatting constraints reduce hallucination but increase prompt length. Expert role conditioning improves domain accuracy but may over-constrain novel problems. Production systems must balance: latency budget vs. reasoning depth, context window vs. instruction density, flexibility vs. reliability.
slides.key_fact: No free lunch — each pattern trades resources for control.
slides.why_it_matters: Architectural decisions require explicit trade-off analysis.

slides.title: Stacking Patterns Without Understanding Interactions
slides.subtitle: More codes ≠ better results. Conflicting signals degrade output.
slides.body: Naive approach: pile on every pattern. Result: model confusion, wasted tokens, unpredictable behavior.
slides.deep_dive: Combining 'be concise' with 'think step by step' creates tension — the model tries to compress its reasoning. 'Be creative' clashes with 'output strict JSON'. 'Act as expert' may override 'admit uncertainty'. Production engineers test pattern combinations like unit tests: isolate, verify, then compose. The robust solution uses minimal, compatible patterns for each task type.
slides.key_fact: Pattern conflicts cause silent degradation, not errors.
slides.why_it_matters: Prevents subtle quality regressions in automated pipelines.

slides.title: How AI Code Review Bots Use These Codes
slides.subtitle: Structured prompts enable reliable, automated PR analysis at scale.
slides.body: Engineering teams embed control codes into prompt templates — not chat sessions.
slides.deep_dive: A code review pipeline uses: role code ('senior security engineer'), reasoning code ('analyze vulnerability class, then impact, then fix'), format code ('output SARIF JSON'), and constraint code ('flag only high/critical'). This template runs on every PR, producing consistent, parseable findings. No human prompting. The 8 codes become API parameters. Latency stays under 3s because patterns are pre-validated and token-optimized.
slides.key_fact: Prompt templates become infrastructure, not conversation.
slides.why_it_matters: Enables AI-as-infrastructure with SLAs, not chat toys.

slides.title: The Complete Control Code Catalog
slides.subtitle: Each code targets a distinct model capability subsystem.
slides.body: Eight orthogonal levers. Combine strategically, not exhaustively.
slides.deep_dive: The 8 codes map to model subsystems: 1) Role Conditioning — primes attention heads for domain. 2) Chain-of-Thought — activates sequential reasoning. 3) Few-Shot Pattern — calibrates output distribution. 4) Structured Format — constrains token probability space. 5) Constraint Declaration — sets hard boundaries. 6) Verification Loop — triggers self-critique. 7) Context Segmentation — isolates task context. 8) Temperature Override — controls entropy per task. Master the subsystem, master the model.
slides.key_fact: Codes are orthogonal — each controls a different mechanism.
slides.why_it_matters: Enables precise behavioral engineering instead of prompt guessing.

slides.title: Start Using Control Codes Today
slides.subtitle: Pick one pattern. Measure. Iterate. Build your prompt library.
slides.body: Stop guessing. Start engineering. Your AI reliability depends on it.
slides.deep_dive: Begin with role + format codes — highest ROI, lowest complexity. Add reasoning for complex tasks. Test each combination like code. Version your prompt templates. Monitor token costs. Treat prompts as compiled artifacts, not chat history. The 8 codes aren't secrets — they're APIs. Use them.
slides.why_it_matters: Separates production AI from demo ware.
